units.title: The modal model
units.editorNote: `Esc` and `Ctrl-[` both return you to Normal mode in Vim. Some hosts claim `Ctrl-[` for themselves, so `Esc` is the one to reach for.

units.title: Cursor movement
units.editorNote: `gj` and `gk` step by screen line, so what they do depends on whether your editor wraps long lines. The distinction itself travels everywhere.

units.title: Entering and changing text
units.editorNote: The Insert-mode `Ctrl` keys are native Vim, but an editor that embeds Vim often claims those chords first, so check the host you are in.

units.title: Operator grammar
units.editorNote: `=` and `gq` reformat using the host's own indent and width settings, so their results vary outside this app. Every other operator here behaves the same anywhere.

units.title: Precision motions and search
units.editorNote: Search and `%` match text, not syntax: they know nothing about your language's semantics. That stays true in every host.

units.title: Text objects
units.editorNote: Text objects read the buffer's own punctuation, so deeply nested or unbalanced code can surprise you. Tag objects also need the host to agree where a tag ends.

units.title: Visual selection
units.editorNote: `Ctrl-v` enters Visual Block in Vim, but Windows and Linux hosts commonly bind it to paste. If it pastes, the host has claimed it.

units.title: Registers and putting
units.editorNote: The `"+` clipboard register is emulated here and never touches your device clipboard. Insert-mode `Ctrl-r` is native Vim, though a host may claim that chord.

units.title: Position memory
units.editorNote: Marks, the jump list, and the change list are all native Vim. An editor that embeds Vim may claim `Ctrl-o` and `Ctrl-i` for its own navigation, so check the host you are in.

units.title: Viewport control
units.editorNote: All of these are native Vim. An editor that embeds Vim may claim the `Ctrl` chords for itself, so check the host you are in.

units.title: Repeatable editing
units.editorNote: `.` behaves the same everywhere. `@:`, `&`, and `:~` repeat Command-line work, so they need a host that runs real Ex commands.

units.title: Command-line ranges and line operations
units.editorNote: Which Ex commands exist, and how they group for undo, varies between Vim and the editors that reimplement it. This app defines and tests the behavior it teaches.

units.title: Substitution and practical regex
units.editorNote: Vim's regex dialect is its own: `\v`, `\zs`, and `\<` are not PCRE. Hosts running a real Vim underneath match it; lighter emulators often do not.

units.title: Macros
units.editorNote: Recording and replaying is native Vim. Some hosts reimplement macros slowly or break undo across a replay, so prefer a real Vim for heavy use.

units.title: Global and Normal automation
units.editorNote: `:global` and `:normal` are where emulators most often fall short of real Vim. Where a host runs Vim underneath, they behave as taught here.

units.title: Real-code workflow capstones
units.editorNote: Nothing new is introduced here. Every command was taught in Units 1–15, and each one's portability caveat travels with it.

units.title: Mastery loops
units.editorNote: A practice surface rather than a lesson. It replays work you have already done, so it inherits each topic's own host caveats.
